To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the practice of extreme sports is a form of green spirituality, 2) it is a way to experience the amplification of the Self, 3) the wilderness is an instrument to strengthen the Self, 4) extreme sports are the attempt to "enter into harmony with nature" and 5) nature is an eschatological dimension.
the extreme sports in the wild are the attempt to experience an amplification of self in order to enter into resonance with nature and become one with it.
the practice of extreme sports in wild nature is a way of "reaching the sacred" and "reaching the self", a way of experiencing an ampliation of the self, of the "I" in order to "be one" with nature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the phenomenon of the "green eschatology" of extreme sports, which, in the context of the contemporary Western culture, is a new way to sacralise the nature.
the analysis of extreme sports and the imagery of wilderness.
the following question: What are the meanings and values associated with extreme sports in the context of wilderness?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nature, in its wildness and inaccessibility, is a powerful and inexhaustible source of meanings.

extreme sports in the wild represent a ritual of "symbolic challenge" to the self, which allows the individual to overcome his or her own limitations and, at the same time, to experience the sacredness of nature.
nature is not a mere object of consumption, but a powerful source of meaning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extreme sportsman, through his physical effort and his ability to overcome the physical limits, is trying to "reconcile himself" with nature.
the "green" spirituality of extreme sports is the result of a process of "naturalization" of the sacred.

of "the green spirit of the wild" which is a sort of nature that, through its implacable laws, allows the self to recognise the "true nature of things", that is the ultimate values of the human being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nature can no longer be considered as the "other" but must be considered as a "self" to be integrated into the human self.
extreme sports are a way to experience a "green eschatology" that allows us to overcome the disorientation of the contemporary world.

extreme sports are an expression of a new green spirituality, which is the result of a process of sacralisation of nature, which in turn is the result of an unprecedented imagery of the natural world.
